Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (textual): Migraine without aura vs tension-type headache; presentation currently most consistent with unilateral left-sided migraine features but tension-type headache remains a plausible contributor given stress/work factors.
- Relevant differential diagnoses and reasoning (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  - Migraine without aura — High likelihood: unilateral left-sided pain, photophobia, onset during sleep, relief with lying down, prior headache history, stress as a trigger.
  - Tension-type headache — Moderate-High likelihood: prominent stress history, frontally focused pain, improvement with rest/relief after lying down; usually bilateral but can be frontally predominant.
  - Dehydration and sleep deprivation-related headache — Moderate likelihood: sleep disruption and hydration discussed as potential contributors.
- If conflict with DDx arises, note: No explicit conflicts identified between transcript and DDx; both migraine and tension-type features are acknowledged in plan.
- Working plan priorities: Provide effective acute relief, address modifiable triggers (sleep, hydration, stress), arrange short-interval follow-up, and consider further testing if not improved.

Management Plan

- Immediate treatment: Ibuprofen as first-line analgesic for possible migraine; continue Paracetamol if tolerated; note: NSAID preferred for migraine management per updated guidelines; dose/spacing to be guided by product labeling and patient tolerance.
- Additional measures: Encourage increased hydration (1.5–2 liters fluid/day excluding caffeinated beverages); aim for 7–8 hours sleep per night; advise reducing work-related stress; consider taking time off work (self-certify for a week) to aid recovery.
- Referrals/therapy: Discuss counselling options; provide link for self-referral to a counseling service; mental health support offered.
- Follow-up: Schedule follow-up in 1 week to reassess symptoms and consider blood tests or alternative diagnoses if not improved.
- Education and safety: Provide notes with danger signs for headaches; advise patient to contact clinic sooner if symptoms worsen or new red flags appear.
- Preventive health follow-up: Preventive issues addressed through counseling and lifestyle modifications; follow-up appointment confirmed.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine without aura — High
  - Justification: Unilateral left-sided headache with photophobia; waking from sleep; previous headache history; stress as trigger; described as severe; partial response to NSAIDs commonly seen in migraines.
  - Likelihood: High
- Tension-type headache — Moderate-High
  - Justification: Significant work-related stress and anxiety history; frontal pain; ability to rest with lying down; typical headaches related to stress.
  - Likelihood: Moderate-High
- Dehydration and sleep deprivation-related headache — Moderate
  - Justification: Sleep disturbance and hydration discussed as contributors; dehydration can provoke headaches; dehydration and fatigue recognized by clinician as potential factors.
  - Likelihood: Moderate
